## 16. Core runtime design

`craftbridge-core` is the universal runtime: it knows how to host a Craft app's session on a phone and nothing about EffectCraft (PD9). Lints: the workspace table every crate inherits, with `unsafe_code` denied — switched off only on the `mod platform` declaration (FX-3's CoreText calls, the memory calls of D-20 when they land, and the capability-bit read of the Android arm64 floor, §23), per `AGENTS.md` §4 — and the never-crash lints (`clippy::unwrap_used`, `panic`, `unimplemented`, `todo` and `unreachable` at `forbid`, `expect_used` at `deny`, and the same calls named by path in `rust/clippy.toml`), stricter than EffectCraft's (`AGENTS.md`, "Never crash").

Every comparison of paths in the journal — the refusal, a take-over, a start's claim that a running export's file lies in a folder another entry names, what a set-aside entry yields to, and one folder's duplicate entries — asks whether two paths name one file as the volume holding them decides, never by their spelling: a file that is there is one with another where they share the file system's device and file number, and a file that is not there is named by the deepest folder that is, together with the names below it folded by that volume's own rules for case and Unicode form, read from the volume and never assumed from the platform — a volume that answers one name to another case answers it, one that answers another Unicode form answers it, and a volume whose rules cannot be read folds every name, so it loses no work — so two exports of one file spelt two ways on a volume that folds the spellings are refused, taken over, claimed and yielded exactly as one spelt one way, while on a volume that keeps the spellings apart `Card.mp4` and `CARD.MP4` are two files, both exports running and each end removing only its own. Every path of a listing holds, a path the second export derives rather than was given holding as much: EffectCraft names a render's log by the output's stem, so two formats of one output name exported at once both write one log, and the second export is refused there, naming it. That refusal is the right answer and not a nuisance to design around, for two exporters writing one log at once leave it no defined file either, and the journal holds no rule that could deal with a file both a running export and the new one will write. The app waits for the export that holds the log, or writes its outputs under names whose logs differ. The engine clears the export's entries when `request_with_progress` returns, whatever its outcome; a call it answers `Cancelled` first deletes what it listed by the rules a start deletes by (below), so a stop that lands after the last frame leaves no finished file for a caller that was told none was made, and a file the disk will not let go of is answered `Io` in its place and stays listed for the next start, while a folder it will not remove, which then holds nothing of the call, stays listed too and, like entries that cannot be cleared once every file has gone, leaves the answer `Cancelled`; a success whose entries cannot be cleared is answered `Io`, since the next start would delete what it wrote. A start in the app's folders (`Engine::start_in(folders, app, gpu)`, or `Engine::start_in_with(folders, build, gpu)`, the start an app crate's constructor makes) prepares the folders, then for each listed entry resolves its folder inside the container and looks at the file without following a link: it deletes a regular file the export wrote, leaves one that is still the file it was when listed (a later queue item, the rest of an older sequence, a kill before the write), refuses `..`, absolute paths, folders, links and anything outside, then removes, the deepest first, each folder of a listed file's path that was not there when the file was listed (the writer makes it, and the journal keeps it apart from the files, in `folders`) once it holds nothing, leaving one that holds anything and refusing one that is now a link or a file, so a killed export leaves the container's folders as it found them, clears the journal and reports it as `Engine::recovery()`; `Engine::start(app, gpu)` keeps no journal. Every write is a temporary file in the same folder renamed over the journal, and the journal is at most 16 MiB; one whose content is no journal names no file, so nothing is deleted and it is replaced; one the disk will not read when a process takes the journal (no export runs then, so it holds no running export's entries) is renamed, unread, to `pending-exports-unread-*.json` beside it, so no export is refused for it, and every later start reads each such file again and, once it reads every one, deals with what they list, removes them and says so in `Engine::recovery()`, while one it cannot read keeps them all waiting; at most 8 wait at once, and past that the unread journal stays where it is, each start deals with nothing and each listing is refused until one can read it; a file that cannot be deleted stays listed, until an export lists its path again and takes the entry over with what was there before, so the next start never deletes the file that export finishes there. A listing never reads the journals set aside, which the disk may still refuse, so it cannot take a set-aside entry over as it lists the path; instead, while a journal waits set aside, the journal keeps, in `taken`, the files of each export that ends other than by a cancel, and a start hands each set-aside entry to the same take-over with those exports as the later listing: the file such an export left is never deleted for the older entry, while a cancelled export has deleted what it wrote and a killed one is still listed, so the set-aside entry deals with what is left, as the entry that took it over would have, and the start names the files whose entries yielded; the journal's own entries are later than every set-aside one, so a start deals with them by their own record even while set-aside journals wait. Any journal may record such an export, which is why a start waits to read them all, and to list their folder: one that reads as no journal may have recorded an export of any file they list, so the journal then records `"every"` and none of those is deleted, while the one that is no journal is replaced, or removed once that is written, and never waits or takes one of the 8 places, past which listings would be refused while it lasted. The record says nothing of when an export ended, so an entry the journal lists after one, and keeps once it is set aside in its turn, yields to it as well, leaving the partial file its killed run wrote: a partial file left costs no work, while a finished one deleted would. The record goes once no journal waits set aside, never while their folder cannot be listed, which may hold some, and it names at most 4096 files, past which it is `"every"` and every set-aside entry of a file yields, so a journal set aside that never reads again cannot grow the journal without end. No set-aside journal expires: one never read may have recorded an export of any file, so letting it go could delete nothing that waiting keeps, and would give up dealing with them all if it reads later. So while one never reads again, the phone keeps, for as long as it stays unreadable, every other set-aside journal waiting with it, the partial files they list, the record and their places of the 8 (once all 8 are taken, a journal the disk will not read at a take stays where it is, as above), and each start says so. Engines of one process share it under one lock, and a start never deletes a file another is writing. A start cannot tell another process's running export from a killed one's, so a process holds an exclusive lock on `pending-exports.lock`, beside the journal, while a start of its own deals with the journal and while exports of its own run with it, from the first listing until the last clears; the system releases it when a process ends, however it ends, and the process lets go of it by unlocking it before it closes its handle, never by the close alone, since the lock belongs to the open file and a process the app starts keeps a copy of every handle the app has open until it runs its program, so a close would leave the lock with that copy and the app's next start or listing would be refused for it. A start that finds another process holding it deals with nothing, a listing that does is refused, and each later start and listing tries again. The lock is held no longer, because iOS terminates a suspended app holding a file lock outside its own data container, as in an App Group container (Apple developer forums, thread 655225). While it holds the lock a process knows what the journal holds, so every listing and clear writes that without reading the file: a journal the disk stops reading mid-run is replaced whole, never set aside with running exports' entries that a later start would act on after they finished; taking the lock again reads the journal again |

**Behaviour.**
1. `start` (called by the app crate's constructor, `start_effects_engine`, through `Engine::start_in_with(folders, build, gpu)` with the app's `GpuChoice`) first checks the processor (`src/platform/cpu.rs`), so that on a phone below the floor no app is built and no folder is touched; then creates the folders if missing, builds the app from them, deals with the files its pending-export journal still lists (D-17, *Returning app* below), builds the GPU device unless `GpuChoice::CpuOnly` (§17: on the engine thread, before the first call, handing the answer to the app's `attach_gpu`), registers the hardware decoders (§18), on Android from the codec list the app handed over before it started, and spawns the actor with the app. Every start names its `GpuChoice`, `Engine::start(app, gpu)` with no folders too, so no engine stays on the CPU because its caller did not choose.
2. Each call becomes a message. Async calls resolve when the actor answers; nothing blocks the caller's thread.
3. A call during an export waits (L3); `info`, progress and cancel are answered at once.
4. `close` stops a running export (as cancel), drops the GPU and surface, and joins the thread. `begin_close` is its half that waits for nothing: it refuses the calls made after it and queues the stop, so the FFI's `shut_down` takes effect in the order it was made and leaves only the join to a thread of its own.

**States.** Starting · Ready · Exporting · CPU only · Closed · Failed to start (§13, d03).
- *Failed to start*: an Android arm64 processor without FP16 → `Unsupported`, naming the missing feature, before the app is built (`Engine::start` and `Engine::start_in`, which take an app already built, refuse it as well, before anything else); folders not writable → `Io`, proven by a probe file in each working folder and none at the top of the container, which holds them all and on an iPhone takes no new file of its own; no GPU with `Preferred` is not a failure (the engine starts on the CPU and `info.gpu` says why).
- *Returning app*: an app relaunched after the system killed it mid-export finds the half-written output. The exporter removes files only on a clean cancel (`crates/engine/src/render_queue.rs:103-106`), so the core's `start` deletes the files its `pending-exports.json` journal still lists that the killed export wrote (listed by the app as the export learns them, before it writes them, and cleared when it ends) (D-17). A call the engine answers `Cancelled` removes what it listed itself, once, in the core, for every export, render and fill, by the same rules, because the exporter's own removal runs only if it sees the stop before it finishes (D-17).

**Edge cases.** A second engine in the same app: allowed, each with its own session and thread; GPU devices are separate. A call after `close`: `Internal { "engine is closed" }`. A progress listener that throws (Swift) or raises (Kotlin): UniFFI reports it as an unexpected callback error; the core ignores it and the export continues.

**Tests.** Unit tests with a fake `CraftApp`: the start with capability bits that lack each half-precision feature, refused in the exact words with the app never built and the folders untouched, and with both bits, started; ordering (L1), calls waiting in order during an export (L3), cancel within one progress interval, panic → `Internal` with the session intact, the pending-export journal on restart.
